main_issue: Whether Agent D may keep wearing a religious thread (covered) under the new no-visible-jewellery rule, or must remove it like everyone else, before the area manager's visit

A-B.evidence: B: 'same for everyone' (T4, T16); A: 'Same for everyone' (T8, T18). At T33 A says arguing isn't helping, slightly distancing, but still same side.

A-C.evidence: C backs covering (T5) and urges A to call/text the manager (T25, T27); A refuses: 'I'm not calling the manager at home' (T26); no compromise reached.

A-D.evidence: A: 'It has to come off... My decision is final' (T8, T22); D: 'It stays on' (T11), 'Then I can't work tomorrow' (T23).

B-C.evidence: B objects to covering (T4); C says covering means not visible (T5); B: 'Why does he get a text?' (T29); C: 'This isn't about you or him' (T30).

B-D.evidence: B: 'That has to come off too' (T2), 'only a problem because he won't follow the rule' (T31); D insists it stays (T11, T15).

C-D.evidence: C: 'If he covers it, then it's not visible' (T5); D: 'Yeah, exactly' (T6); C pushes to warn the manager so D can work (T25).
